text: Given a tenant with print queues, when printix_list_printers is called, then the response lists the tenant's queues (id, name, status, site_id), paginated, with has_more set when more exist than the page size.
Given a printer/queue id that exists in the tenant, when printix_get_printer is called with that id, then the response contains that printer's full properties and capabilities.
Given a site, workstation, or printer id that does not exist in the tenant, when the matching get tool is called, then the response is a structured not_found error, not a crash or an unhandled 500.
Given a request with no X-Printix-Client-Id/X-Printix-Client-Secret headers, when any printix_* tool is called, then the HTTP response is 401 and the body lists the required header names.

Given credential headers that Printix itself rejects (invalid client_id/secret), when any printix_* tool is called, then the tool returns a structured unauthorized error (distinct from TC4's transport-level 401), not a 500.
Given a credential pair that can see exactly one Printix tenant and no X-Printix-Tenant-Id header, when any printix_* tool is called, then the tenant is auto-resolved and the call proceeds normally.

Given a credential pair that can see more than one Printix tenant and no X-Printix-Tenant-Id header, when any printix_* tool is called, then the response is a structured invalid_argument error listing the tenant ids found, not a silent guess.
Given a tenant with zero printers (or sites, or workstations), when the matching list tool is called, then the response is an empty list, not an error.

Given two simulated concurrent requests using two different tenants' credentials, when each calls printix_list_printers, then each response contains only its own tenant's data and the per-request context is reset afterward (no leakage via shared state).

Given two real Printix tenants' credentials, when each is used against a running instance back-to-back, then each response only ever contains that tenant's own printers — confirms TC9's unit-level proof against the real API.
steps: Obtain client_id/client_secret for two distinct real Printix tenants
Call printix_list_printers with tenant A's headers against the running service
Call printix_list_printers with tenant B's headers against the same running service
expect: Tenant A's response lists only tenant A's printers; tenant B's response lists only tenant B's printers; no overlap or cross-tenant data.
evidence: needs a real vendor account — no Printix trial/test tenant is available to this pipeline; not a release blocker per vendor-mcp-development SOP ("no test account also ships to INT").

text: Given the service is running, when GET /health is called, then it returns 200 without requiring any Printix credential headers and without calling the Printix API.

Given one real Printix tenant, when initialize -> tools/list -> tools/call printix_list_printers is run against it, then the returned data shape matches what api.printix.net actually returns (confirms the mocked unit tests reflect reality).
steps: Obtain client_id/client_secret for one real Printix tenant with at least one printer
Start the service locally with those credentials in the request headers
Call initialize, then tools/list, then tools/call printix_list_printers
Compare the response fields against the live Printix Cloud Print API response
expect: Tool catalogue includes all 6 printix_* tools; printix_list_printers returns real queue data whose fields match this design's §5 contract.
evidence: needs a real vendor account — see TC10; not a release blocker.
